svg.text: The SMART Study · set-up guide
Route C: Your child has an Android phone, and you have an Android or iPhone
Get the Family Link app
2 minutes · on your phone
1. Open the Play Store (Android) or the App Store
(iPhone).
2. Search for Family Link and install it.
3. Open it and sign in with your own Google Account
(often ending in @gmail.com).

g.text: Set screen time limits · Manage apps
Sign in with your own Google Account to

svg.text: Add your child's Google
Account
10 minutes · on your phone, in Family Link
1. If they don't have one, choose No and follow the
prompts to create one: their name, date of birth, a
Gmail address and a password.
2. – Check the date of birth is correct. Google uses
your child's age to decide which protections apply.
A wrong birth year quietly switches off protections
you think you have.
3. – Write down the new address and password. You'll
need them on your child's phone in the next step.
4. If they already have one, choose Yes and follow the
prompts. Check the date of birth on their account is
correct too.
5. After you set the password, read what Google shows
you and tap to agree.
6. Google then checks it's you. You may get a code by
text message, and you may be asked for a card's
details to confirm you're over 18. You won't be
charged.
7. Family Link shows you what it can do. Tap through to
the end.
8. At Choose settings for your child, choose fewer
steps. You'll make the study's settings later in
this guide.
9. When asked about personalising your data, you can
tap Reject all.

g.text: You need one for your child to supervise
You can change these at any time.
Choose whether Google uses Alex's activity

svg.text: Link your child's phone
10 minutes · on your child's phone
1. On your child's phone, open Settings and tap Google
(on some phones: Google services). You don't need
anything called All services.
2. Tap Parental controls. It's under Kids & family (on
Samsung phones: Children and family).
3. Tap Get started, choose Child or teen, then choose
your child's account.
4. When asked for a parent, sign in with your own
Google Account. This only confirms it's you.
5. If asked, set a parental controls PIN: four digits
your child doesn't know. Write it down with your
other codes, and don't let your child see you type
it.
6. You'll be asked about lots of other settings along
the way. Go straight through: accepting them all or
saying no to them all are both fine, because you'll
make the study's settings next.
7. Your child enters their own password and taps Agree.
8. On a Samsung phone, you may also be asked to set up
parental controls with a Samsung account. If so:
9. – Sign in on their phone with your own Samsung
account. If you don't have one, you can create one
there, even if your own phone isn't a Samsung.
10. – Go to Family → Invite new members → Create child
account, and use your child's Google (Gmail)
address.
11. – Your Samsung account can stay on their phone. Your
Google Account must not.

g.text: Set up Family Link to supervise this phone:
set screen time limits, manage apps and
Choose who you are setting up parental
A parent needs to sign in to supervise this
Your parent will be able to manage apps, set
screen time limits and see this phone's

svg.text: Allow only the apps on the
list
10 minutes · on your phone, in Family Link
1. Open Family Link and tap Screen time. You don't need
to go into Controls.
2. – If it asks you to Add device, your child's phone
isn't linked yet. Follow the instructions it shows:
they're the same as in Link your child's phone.
3. – Otherwise you'll see your child's phone, shown by
its model name (for example SM-S901B).
4. Under Schedules there are two options, Downtime and
School time. Turn on Downtime.
5. Tap Weekly schedule → choose a day → Start 12:00 AM,
End 11:59 PM → Apply to all days of the week.
6. Tap Allowed apps. There's no switch to allow them
all at once, so go through the apps on the list one
at a time and set each one to Unlimited time.

g.text: Google Play, Chrome and Web, YouTube
Daily limit and limits for each app
Apply to all days of the week

svg.text: Allow only the websites they
need
5 minutes · on your phone, in Family Link
1. In Family Link, go to Controls → Google Chrome and
Web.
2. Choose Only allow approved sites.
3. Tap Approved sites and add each site on the list.
Use the main web address only, such as bbc.co.uk.
Family Link won't accept a page within a site, such
as bbc.co.uk/bitesize.
4. If other browsers aren't already blocked, block
them: Screen time → Time limits → tap each browser →
turn Allowed off.
If a homework site won't load, don't switch the filter off.
Email smartphonestudy@public.io and we'll add it to the
shared list.

g.text: Which websites your child can visit
Add the sites on the list

svg.text: Lock the settings
3 minutes · on your phone, in Family Link
1. In Family Link, go to Controls → Google Play.
2. Under download approvals, choose All content, so
nothing new can be installed without your approval.

g.text: Which websites your child can visit
Approval needed for free and paid downlo…

svg.text: Check it worked
2 minutes · on your phone
1. In Family Link, open your child's profile.
2. If it shows their phone and recent activity, the
link is live.
3. If it shows nothing after a few hours, check the
phone is switched on, connected, and signed into the
supervised account.
